candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care — Information Technology, printed p.22 / PDF p.26: utilize information technology resources, enter documentation accurately/completely/timely, and use resources to promote quality client care
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — Information Technology / EHR downtime contingency
candidate.educational_objective: Use the facility's established EHR downtime process to maintain safe, continuous documentation and care during electronic-system outages.

options.A: Activate the facility's approved downtime procedure and use the designated backup documentation/order process, such as approved paper forms
options.B: Stop documenting client care until the electronic system is restored
options.C: Rely on memory and recreate all assessments and medication-related documentation after the system returns
options.D: Create an informal personal documentation system that is not part of the facility's downtime plan

candidate.rationale: Current federal Health IT SAFER guidance emphasizes contingency planning for planned and unplanned EHR unavailability. HealthIT.gov specifically notes that practices should have a well-designed backup process, including paper-based documentation and ordering when the EHR is unavailable. Therefore the nurse should follow the facility's approved downtime procedure rather than delay documentation, rely on memory, or improvise an unauthorized record system.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Health care organizations should have established contingency procedures for EHR downtime, including backup documentation/order processes such as paper-based systems.
candidate.source_document_title: SAFER Guides — Contingency Planning; Health IT Playbook — Quality & Patient Safety
